Benefit: What has been reported concerning encouragement to learn the obligatory shares (fara'id) and to teach them is what al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Learn the fara'id and teach them to the people, for I am a man who will be taken away, and knowledge will be taken away, and trials will appear, until two people dispute over an inheritance share and cannot find anyone to judge between them." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Learn the fara'id and teach them, for it is half of knowledge, and it will be forgotten, and it is the first thing to be removed from my community."

Reports from Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Anas have also been narrated encouraging the study of the fara'id, and likewise from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) and those after them.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 4, verse 11–14 (part 1 of 3):

This is an elaboration of what was stated in summary in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾ [an-Nisa: 7], and it has been cited as evidence for the permissibility of delaying clarification (ta'khir al-bayan) beyond the time of need. This verse is a pillar of the religion, a foundation of its rulings, and a "mother" of verses (umm min ummahat al-ayat), because it comprises what is important of the science of the obligatory shares (ilm al-fara'id, the science of inheritance). This science was among the most noble of the sciences of the Companions, and most of their disputes were concerned with it. After completing the explanation of what the word of God contains of the obligatory shares, I will mention, God willing, some of the virtues of this science.

His words: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾, meaning: concerning the clarification of their inheritance.

The scholars differed on whether the children of children (awlad al-awlad) are included or not. The Shafi'is said: they are included metaphorically (majazan), not literally (haqiqatan). The Hanafis said: the word "children" (awlad) literally includes them when there are no children of the loins (awlad al-sulb). There is no disagreement that the sons' sons are like sons in inheritance when the sons are absent; this disagreement concerns only whether the word "children" denotes their children when the sons are absent. The word "children" includes one of them who is a disbeliever, though he is excluded by the Sunnah; likewise the one who kills intentionally is included, though he is excluded by the Sunnah and consensus (ijma'); and the hermaphrodite (khunha) is included. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agreed that he inherits according to the place from which he urinates. If he urinates from both, then according to whichever came first. If the urine came out from both without one preceding the other, he has half the share of a male and half the share of a female. It was said: he is given the lesser of the two shares, which is the share of a female; this was said by Yahya ibn Adam, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i.

This verse abrogates what existed in the early days of Islam of inheritance through alliance (al-hilf), emigration (al-hijrah), and contract (al-mu'aqadah). The scholars have agreed that if there is with the children someone who has a defined share (fard musamma), he is given it, and what remains of the property goes to the male, equal to the share of two females, based on the established hadith in the Sahihayn and others, in the wording: "Give the obligatory shares to their rightful owners, and whatever remains is for the nearest male relative," unless he is excluded in their presence, such as the uterine brothers (al-ikhwa li-umm). His words: ﴿For the male, the like of the share of two females﴾ is a resumptive sentence (jumlah mustaanifah) explaining the bequest concerning the children, so a pronoun referring back to them must be supposed: "God enjoins you concerning your children: for the male among them is the like of the share of two females."

What is meant is when males and females come together. As for when they are alone: the male has the entire inheritance, the female has half, and two or more females have two-thirds. His words: ﴿If they are women above two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾, meaning: if they are the children, the feminine form being in accordance with the predicate, or the daughters, or the offspring are women with no male with them, above two, that is, exceeding two. The phrase "above two" is either a qualifier of "women" or a second predicate of "was" (kana): ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾, the deceased being implied by the context.

The apparent sense of the Qur'anic wording is that two-thirds is the obligatory share of three or more daughters. It does not specify an obligatory share for two, and therefore the people of knowledge differed about their share. The majority held that when the two stand apart from sons, they have two-thirds. Ibn Abbas held that their obligatory share is one-half. The majority argued by analogy (qiyas) with the two sisters, for God, Exalted is He, said concerning them: ﴿If they are two, then for them is two-thirds﴾ [an-Nisa: 176], so they joined the two daughters to the two sisters in entitlement to two-thirds, just as they joined sisters exceeding two to daughters in sharing the two-thirds. It was also said that the verse contains what indicates that two daughters have two-thirds, because when one female with her brother has a third, two daughters when alone have two-thirds. This argument was used by Isma'il ibn Ayyash and al-Mubarrad. Al-Nahhas said: This argument is an error in the view of the people of reasoning, because the disagreement concerns two daughters when they stand apart from sons. Moreover, the opponent may say: if he leaves two daughters and a son, the two daughters have one-half; this is evidence that this is their obligatory share. The argument of the majority can be supported by the fact that when God obligated for a single daughter standing alone one-half, by His words: ﴿And if she is one, then for her is one-half﴾, the obligatory share of two daughters standing alone exceeds that of the one; and analogy with the two sisters required restricting the two daughters to two-thirds.

It was said: the word "above" (fawq) is superfluous, and the meaning is: "if they are two women," as in His words: ﴿strike above the necks﴾ [al-Anfal: 12], meaning "the necks." Al-Nahhas and Ibn Atiyyah rejected this and said: it is an error, because adverbs and all nouns are not permitted in the speech of the Arabs to be added without meaning. Ibn Atiyyah said: Moreover, His words ﴿above the necks﴾ are the eloquent form, and "above" is not superfluous; rather it carries a determined meaning, because the blow to the neck must fall above the bones at the joint, not on the brain, as Durayd ibn al-Simmah said: "Lower it below the brain and raise it above the bone; thus I used to strike the necks of heroes," end of quotation. Furthermore, if the word "above" were superfluous, as they claim, it would say: "then for the two of them is two-thirds of what he left," and not "then for them is two-thirds of what he left."

The strongest thing the majority can cite is what Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Jabir, who said: "The wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, these are the two daughters of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', whose father was killed with you at Uhud as a martyr, and their paternal uncle took their property and left them no property, and they cannot be married unless they have property. He said: God will decide in this matter. Then the verse of inheritance was revealed: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾, the verse. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to their uncle and said: Give the two daughters of Sa'd two-thirds, their mother one-eighth, and what remains is for you." They related it through several chains from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir. al-Tirmidhi said: It is not known except from his narration.

His words: ﴿And if she is one, then for her is one-half﴾. Nafi' and the people of Madinah read "wahidatun" (one) in the nominative, with "kana" as a complete verb meaning: "if one exists," or "if one comes into being." The rest read it in the accusative. Al-Nahhas said: This is a good reading, meaning: if the one left behind or the one born is a single female.

His words: ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is the sixth﴾. This means the parents of the deceased, and it is a pronoun referring to something not mentioned, which is permissible because the context implies it. "To each one of them is the sixth" is a substitute (badal) for His words "and for his parents," by repetition of the governing element for emphasis and clarification.

Al-Hasan and Nu'aym ibn Maysarah read "al-sudsu" (the sixth) with a sukun on the dal, and likewise they read al-thuluth (the third) and al-rub' (the quarter) up to al-'ushr (the tenth) with sukun. This is the dialect of Banu Tamim and Rabi'ah. The majority read with a vowel (harakah), a damma, which is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and Banu Asad for all of them. The meaning of "the two parents" is the father and the mother, and the dual is in the form of the word "father" by way of prevalence (taghlib).

The scholars differed about the grandfather: is he in the position of the father, so that the brothers are excluded by him, or not? Abu Bakr al-Siddiq held that he is in the position of the father, and none of the Companions opposed him during his caliphate. They differed on this after his death. Those who agreed with Abu Bakr's view were: Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Aisha, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Hanifah, Abu Thawr and Ishaq. They argued from such words as His saying: ﴿the religion of your father Abraham﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], and His saying: ﴿O children of Adam﴾ [al-A'raf: 26, 27, 31, 35], and His words, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Shoot, O sons of Isma'il." Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn Mas'ud held that the grandfather inherits along with the brothers of full or paternal blood, and he does not reduce them from the third; and with the sharers (dhawu al-furud) he does not reduce from the sixth, according to the view of Zayd, Malik, al-Awza'i, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and al-Shafi'i. It was said: the grandfather shares with the brothers up to the sixth, and he does not reduce it by any amount with the sharers and others; this is the view of Ibn Abi Layla and a group.

The majority held that the grandfather excludes the children of the brothers. Al-Sha'bi related from Ali that he treated the children of brothers in the division (al-qasimah) as brothers. The scholars agreed that the grandfather inherits nothing alongside the father, and they agreed that the grandmother has the sixth when the deceased has no mother, and they agreed that the father does not exclude the maternal grandmother (umm al-umm).

They differed concerning the inheritance of the grandmother when her son is alive. It is related from Zayd ibn Thabit, Uthman and Ali that she does not inherit when her son is alive, and this was the view of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Abu Thawr and the people of opinion. It is related from Umar, Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Musa that she inherits alongside him; it is also related from Ali and Uthman, and this was the view of Shurayh, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ubaydullah ibn al-Hasan, Shurayk, Ahmad, Ishaq and Ibn al-Mundhir.

His words: ﴿If he has a child﴾. The word "child" (walad) applies to both male and female. But if the child present is a male alone or with a female among them, the grandfather has only the sixth. If the child present is a female, the grandfather has the sixth as a fixed share and is an agnatic heir (asabah) for what exceeds the sixth. The children of a deceased son are like the children of the deceased. His words: ﴿But if he has no child﴾, meaning: nor a son's child, due to the consensus mentioned before, ﴿and his parents inherit from him﴾, alone apart from all other heirs, as the majority held, that the mother does not take a third of the estate except when the deceased has no heir other than the two parents. As for when one of the spouses is with them, the mother has only a third of what remains after the existing spouse's share.

It is related from Ibn Abbas that the mother has a third of the original estate when one of the spouses is present, which entails preferring the mother over the father in the case of a spouse and two parents, with agreement that the father is superior to her when they stand alone apart from one of the spouses. His words: ﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is the sixth﴾. The unqualified word "brothers" indicates that there is no difference between brothers of full blood or of one parent.

The people of knowledge have agreed that two brothers stand in the place of three or more in excluding the mother to the sixth, except what is related from Ibn Abbas, that he made two as one in not excluding. They also agreed that two or more sisters are like two brothers in excluding the mother.

His words: ﴿after a bequest he makes, or a debt﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Asim read "yusa" (bequeathed) with a fatha on the sad. The rest read it with a kasra. Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the kasra, because the deceased was mentioned before this.

Al-Akhfash said: Confirmation of this is His words: "yusina" and "tusuna." Scholars differed on the reason the bequest is mentioned before the debt, though the debt is by consensus prior to it. It was said: the intent is to place both before the inheritance without intending an order between them. It was said: since the bequest is less binding than the debt, it is mentioned first out of concern for it. It was said: it is mentioned first because it occurs frequently, so it became like a matter binding on every deceased. It was said: it is mentioned first because it is the share of the needy and the poor, while the debt is placed later because it is the share of a creditor who demands it with strength and authority. It was said: since the bequest arises from the deceased himself, it is mentioned first, unlike the debt, which is established and must be paid whether mentioned or not. It was said: it is mentioned first because it resembles inheritance in being taken without return, so it may be hard for the heirs to carry out, unlike the debt, since their souls are at rest about paying it. This bequest is restricted by His words: ﴿without causing harm﴾, as will come, God willing.

**His words, "Your fathers and your sons; you know not which of them is nearer to you in benefit":** It has been said that the predicate of "your fathers and your sons" is omitted, meaning "they are the ones for whom the shares are apportioned." It has also been said that the predicate is his words "you know not," and what follows it, while "nearer" is the predicate. His words "which of them" and "in benefit" are a *tamyiz* (a specifying accusative, which clarifies the ambiguity of the preceding term). The meaning is: you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit, through supplicating for you and giving charity on your behalf, as in the authentic hadith, "or a righteous child who supplicates for him." Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said: "A son may be superior, so that he is allowed to intercede for his father."

Some exegetes said: If the son is of higher rank than his father in the Hereafter, he asks Allah to raise his father up to him; and if the father is of higher rank than his son, he asks Allah to raise his son up to him. It has also been said: the intended benefit is in this world and the Hereafter, as said by Ibn Zayd. It has also been said that the meaning is: you do not know who among your fathers and sons is most beneficial to you, the one who made a bequest and thereby directed you to the reward of the Hereafter by executing his bequest, so that he is nearer to you in benefit, or the one who left no bequest and left you abundant worldly wealth? Sahib al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) strengthened this view, saying: "Because the sentence is parenthetical (*i'tiradiyyah*), and it is proper for a parenthetical clause to emphasise what it interrupts. This is consistent with his words, 'an obligation from Allah,' which is in the accusative as an emphatic infinitive (*masdar mu'akkid*), since the meaning of 'He enjoins you' is 'He imposes upon you.'" Makki and others said: it is an emphatic circumstantial clause (*hal mu'akkidah*), and its governing element is "He enjoins you."

The first view is preferable. **"Indeed Allah is ever Knowing"** of the distribution of inheritances, **"Wise,"** who ordained their distribution and clarified it to its rightful recipients. Al-Zajjaj said: Knowing of things before He created them, Wise in what He decrees and executes concerning them.

**His words, "And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child":** The address here is to the men. By "child" is meant a child of the loins or a grandchild, based on the consensus we mentioned earlier. **"But if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave":** This is agreed upon. The scholars did not differ that the husband, in the absence of a child, receives one half, and in the presence of a child, however remote, receives one quarter.

**His words, "after any bequest" etc.:** the discussion of it is as previously stated.

**His words, "And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave":** This share with a child and the share without a child are such that a single wife may take it alone, and more than one wife share it. There is no disagreement on this. The discussion of bequest and debt is as previously stated.

**His words, "And if a man leaves an inheritance as *kalala*":** By "man" is meant the deceased. *Yuwarathu* is in the passive voice, from *waritha* and not *awratha*, and it is the predicate of *kana*. *Kalalatan* is a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in *yuwarathu*, meaning: "is inherited while being in a state of *kalala*." Or the predicate is *kalalatun* and *yuwarathu* is a qualifier of *rajulun*, meaning: "if a man who is inherited is one who is *kala*lah, having neither child nor parent."

It is also read as *yuwarathu* (lightened) and *yuwarrathu* (intensified). Then *kalalatan* is an object or a circumstantial accusative, with the object omitted, meaning: "is inherited, and the intention is that he is in a state of *kalala*," or it is an object of purpose, meaning: "for the sake of *kalala*." *Kalala* is a verbal noun from *takallalahu al-nasab*, meaning the lineage encompassed him, and from it the crown (*iklil*) is named, because it encircles the head.

It refers to the deceased who has no child and no parent. This is the view of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, 'Ali, and the majority of scholars, and it is what the author of the *Kitab al-'Ayn*, Abu Mansur al-Lughawi, Ibn 'Arafa, al-Qutaybi, Abu 'Ubayd, and Ibn al-Anbari said. It has been said that this is a consensus.

Ibn Kathir said: This is the view of the people of Madina, Kufa, and Basra, and it is the view of the seven jurists and the four imams, and of the majority of later and earlier scholars, indeed of all of them. More than one person has reported the consensus on it, and a hadith traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) has been related about it. End of quotation.

Abu Hatim and al-Athram related from Abu 'Ubayda that he said: "*Kalala* is everyone who is not inherited by a father, a son, or a brother, and this is *kalala* according to the Arabs." Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Abu 'Ubayda's mention here of the brother alongside the father and son as conditions of *kalala* is an error with no basis, and no one else mentioned it as a condition of *kalala*. What is related from Abu Bakr and 'Umar, that *kalala* is only one who has no child, they both retracted.

Ibn Zayd said: *Kalala* refers to both the living and the dead together. They named relatives *kalala* because they surround the deceased on his sides while not being part of him, nor he of them, unlike the son and father, who are his two extremities; when they are gone, lineage encircles him. It has been said that *kalala* is derived from *kalal*, meaning fatigue, as if the inheritance reaches the heir from afar and with exertion. Ibn al-A'rabi said: *kalala* is the distant paternal cousins.

In sum: whoever reads *yuwarrithu* (with a kasra on the *ra'* and shadda) (this is some of the Kufans), or *yuwarithu* (lightened, read by al-Hasan and Ayyub), takes *kalala* to mean relatives. Whoever reads *yuwarathu* with a fatha on the *ra'* (this is the majority), it is possible that *kalala* means the deceased, and it is possible that it means the relatives. It has been related from 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Sha'bi that *kalala* is whatever is other than a child and a parent among the heirs.

al-Tabari said: The correct view is that *kalala* are those who inherit the deceased apart from his child and parent, because of the soundness of the report of Jabir: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, only *kalala* inherit from me; shall I bequeath all my wealth?' He said, 'No.'" End of quotation. It is related from 'Ata' that he said: *kalala* is the wealth.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: This is a weak view with no basis. The author of the *Kashshaf* said: *kalala* applies to three things: to one who leaves neither child nor parent; to one among those left behind who is neither child nor parent; and to relatives other than through child or parent. End of quotation.

**His words, "or a woman":** it is conjoined to "a man" and bound by the same restriction; that is: "or a woman who is inherited as *kalala*."

**His words, "and he has a brother or a sister":** Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas read *min umm* ("from the mother"). The mention of who related that from him will come later.

Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars have agreed that the brothers here are the brothers on the mother's side. He said: There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that the full brothers or the paternal brothers do not receive this share. Their consensus indicates that the brothers mentioned in His words, "And if they are brothers and sisters, men and women, then the male has the equal share of two females" [4:176], are full brothers or paternal brothers. The pronoun in His words, "and he has a brother or a sister," is singular because each of them is intended, as is the custom of the Arabs when they mention two nouns equal in rule: they may use a singular pronoun referring to both, as in His words, "And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome" and His words, "those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah." They may also use a dual pronoun, as in His words, "If he is rich or poor, Allah is more entitled to both of them" [4:135].

We have previously given a discussion on this longer than what is mentioned here.

**His words, "But if they are more than that, they are partners in the third":** The reference of "that" in His words is to "and he has a brother or a sister," meaning: more than a single brother alone or a single sister alone. This applies when there are two or more, whether two males, two females, or a male and a female. It has been used as evidence that the male is like the female among the maternal siblings, since Allah made them partners in the third without mentioning the male's superiority over the female, as He mentioned for children and full or paternal siblings. Al-Qurtubi said: This is a consensus.

The verse indicates that when the maternal siblings complete the division, they take precedence over the full or paternal siblings. This applies in the case known as *al-himariyya* (the donkey problem), where the deceased leaves a husband, a mother, two maternal brothers, and full brothers. The husband receives one half, the mother one sixth, the two maternal brothers one third, and the full brothers receive nothing. The reasoning is that the condition under which the siblings on the mother's side inherit has been met, namely that the deceased is a *kalala*. This is supported by the hadith: "Give the fixed shares to their rightful owners, and what remains goes to the nearest male," which is in the two *Sahihs* and elsewhere. We have established the indication of the verse and the hadith on this in the treatise we named *al-Mabahith al-Durriyya fi al-Mas'ala al-Himariyya*. On this question there has been disagreement among the Companions and those after them, which is well known.

**His words, "after any bequest which is made or a debt":** the discussion of it is as previously stated.

**His words, "not causing harm":** that is, he makes the bequest while not harming his heirs in any form of harm, such as acknowledging something that is not owed, or making a bequest with no purpose except to harm the heirs, or bequeathing to an heir absolutely, or bequeathing to someone else more than a third when the heirs have not permitted it. This restriction, namely His words "not causing harm," refers back to the bequest and the debt mentioned, so it qualifies both. Thus any acknowledgments of debts or bequests that are forbidden, or whose owner intends nothing but to harm his heirs, are null and rejected, and nothing of them is executed, neither a third nor less. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agreed that a bequest to an heir is not permitted. End of quotation. This restriction, namely the absence of harm, qualifies everything mentioned earlier concerning bequest and debt. Abu al-Su'ud said in his commentary: The restriction is specified for this context because heirs are the usual object of the deceased's neglect of their rights.

**His words, "as a bequest from Allah":** it is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: He enjoins you with this as a bequest from Allah, like His words, "an obligation from Allah." Ibn 'Atiyya said: It is also valid for "not causing harm" to govern it, meaning that harm falls upon it or because of it, so the bequest is figuratively treated as the one harmed; on this view the bequest is an object, because the active participle has relied on its described noun or because it carries negation in meaning. al-Hasan read *wasiyyatin min Allah* with the genitive, making the active participle an adjunct to it, as in the phrase "O thief of the night of the people of the house."

That this bequest is from Allah, glory be to Him, is evidence that He has bequeathed to His servants these detailed provisions mentioned in the shares, and that every bequest from His servants that contradicts them is preceded by the bequest of Allah. This includes bequests that favour some heirs over others, or that involve harm in any form. The reference of "that" in His words, "those," is to the rulings mentioned earlier, which He called *hudud* (limits), because they may not be exceeded and their transgression is not permitted. **"And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger"** in the division of inheritances and other legal rulings, as the generality of the wording indicates, **"He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow."**

Similarly His words, **"And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger"**: Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *nudkhilhu* with the nun. The rest read it with the yā'.

**His words, "And for him is a humiliating punishment":** that is, after his admission to the Fire, there is a punishment whose true nature is unknown. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others related from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me, and I said, 'What do you command me to do with my wealth, O Messenger of Allah?' Then this was revealed."

We have already mentioned that the occasion of revelation was the question of the wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi, who said: The people of the Jahiliyya did not give inheritance to young girls or weak boys; no man inherited from his children except one who could fight. So 'Abd al-Rahman, the brother of the poet Hassan, died and left a wife called Umm Kuhha and five slave-girls. The heirs took his wealth, so Umm Kuhha complained of this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse: "And if they are women above two," and then, concerning Umm Kuhha, He said: "And for them is a quarter of what you leave."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when he led us on a path, we followed him and found it easy. He was asked about a woman and her two parents, and he said: for the wife is a quarter, for the mother one third of what remains, and what remains (p. 279) goes to the father.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 4, verses 11–14 (part 3 of 3):

Abd al-Razzaq and al-Bayhaqi also narrated a similar report from Zayd ibn Thabit. Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim (who declared it sound), and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas that he entered upon Uthman and said: "Two brothers do not reduce the mother's share to a third." God says: ﴿But if he has siblings﴾, and "two brothers" is not "siblings" in the language of your people. Uthman said: "I cannot reverse what was decided before me, which has spread through the cities and by which people have inherited." Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan also narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit that he said: "The Arabs call two brothers 'siblings' (ikhwa)."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud, al-Daraqutni, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ali, who said: "You recite this verse, ﴿after any bequest he may have made or debt﴾, but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) settled the debt before the bequest, and the full siblings (a'yan bani al-umm) inherit to the exclusion of the half-siblings through the father (bani al-allat)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding God's words: ﴿Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾, that he said: "The most obedient to God among fathers and sons, the highest in rank with God on the Day of Resurrection, because God, glorified is He, grants intercession to the believers for one another."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding God's words ﴿nearer to you in benefit﴾, that he said: "In this world."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Darimi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that he used to read: (And he has a brother or a sister from the mother).

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: "None of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) ever gave the siblings from the mother any share alongside the grandfather (al-jadd)."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Shihab, who said: "Umar decided that the inheritance of the siblings from the mother is shared equally among them, males and females alike." He said: "I do not think Umar decided this until he learned it from the Messenger of God, and also from this verse, in which God says: ﴿But if they are more than that, they share in the third﴾."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Causing harm in a bequest is among the major sins." Then he recited: ﴿without causing harm﴾. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from him as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet).

In its chain is Umar ibn al-Mughira Abu Hafs al-Misisi. Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir said: "He is known as the mufti of the poor (Mufti al-Masakin), and many imams narrated from him." Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "He is a shaykh." Ali ibn al-Madini said: "He is unknown; I do not know him." Ibn Jarir said: "The sound version is the mawquf (stopping at a Companion)." The men of the chain of this mawquf report are the men of the Sahih, for al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan from Ali ibn Hujr, from Ali ibn Musharr, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrima, from him (Ibn Abbas).

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn Majah (the wording is his), and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A man may act with the deeds of the people of goodness for seventy years, then when he makes a bequest he deviates in it, so he is sealed with the worst of his deeds and enters the Fire. And a man may act with the deeds of the people of evil for seventy years, then he is just in his bequest, so he is sealed with the best of his deeds and enters Paradise." Then Abu Hurayra said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿These are the limits of God﴾ up to His words ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾." In its chain is Shahr ibn Hawshab, about whom there is a well-known discussion.

Ibn Majah narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever cuts off the inheritance of his heir, God will cut off his inheritance from Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab (Branches of Faith) narrated it from a hadith of Abu Hurayra as a marfu' report.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated from Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said," and he mentioned something similar.

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to visit him during his illness and he said: "I have much wealth, and no one inherits from me except a daughter of mine. Should I give charity with two-thirds?" He said: "No." He said: "Then half?" He said: "No." He said: "Then a third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much. It is better that you leave your heirs wealthy than that you leave them poor, begging from people."

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "God has given you charity from a third of your wealth as an increase in your good deeds," meaning the bequest.

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I wish people had reduced the third to a quarter, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The third is much.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Ibn Umar, who said: "The third was mentioned in the presence of Umar regarding bequests, and he said: 'The third is moderate, neither stingy nor excessive.'" Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Ali, who said: "For me to bequeath a fifth is dearer to me than to bequeath a quarter, and for me to bequeath a quarter is dearer to me than to bequeath a third. Whoever bequeaths a third has not left anything out."

Benefit: What has been reported concerning encouragement to learn the obligatory shares (fara'id) and to teach them is what al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Learn the fara'id and teach them to the people, for I am a man who will be taken away, and knowledge will be taken away, and trials will appear, until two people dispute over an inheritance share and cannot find anyone to judge between them." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Learn the fara'id and teach them, for it is half of knowledge, and it will be forgotten, and it is the first thing to be removed from my community."

Reports from Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Anas have also been narrated encouraging the study of the fara'id, and likewise from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) and those after them.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 4, verses 15–18:

When the Exalted, in this surah, mentioned kindness towards women, delivering their dowries to them and their inheritance alongside men, He mentioned the severity against them for what they may commit of immorality, lest they imagine that it permits them to abandon chastity. Al-lati (اللاتي) is the plural of allati (التي) according to meaning, not form. It has several dialectal forms: allati with the ta and ya, allat with the ya dropped and the kasra kept to indicate it, allai (اللائي) with a hamza and ya, and allā (اللاء) with a kasra on the hamza and the ya dropped. In the plural of the plural, it is said al-lawati (اللواتي), al-lawai (اللوائي), al-lawat (اللوات), and al-lawa' (اللواء).

Al-fahisha (الفاحشة) is the ugly deed; it is a verbal noun like al-'afiya and al-'aqiba. Ibn Mas'ud read bil-fahisha (بالفاحشة). What is meant here specifically is adultery (zina), and ityan (إتيان) of it means committing it and engaging in it.

By His words "from your women" (من نسائكم) is meant the Muslim women, and likewise "from you" (منكم) is meant the Muslims. His words "confine them to the houses" (فأمسكوهن في البيوت) were at the beginning of Islam, then abrogated by His words, "The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each of them" (الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا). Some scholars held that the mentioned confinement and likewise the harm remain alongside the flogging, because there is no contradiction between them and combining them is possible.

His words "or God makes a way for them" (أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا) refer to what is in the authentic hadith of 'Ubada, where the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, God has made a way for them: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year," and so on. His words "and the two of you who commit it among you" (واللذان يأتيانها منكم): al-ladhani (اللذان) is the dual of al-ladhi, and the analogical form would have been al-ladhayan, like rahayan.

Sibawayh said: the ya was dropped to distinguish declinable nouns from indeclinable demonstrative nouns. Abu 'Ali said: the ya was dropped for lightness.

Ibn Kathir read al-ladhanni (اللذانّ) with a doubled nun, which is the dialect of Quraysh. There is another dialect, al-ladha (اللذا), with the nun dropped. The rest read al-ladhani with a single nun. Sibawayh said: the meaning is "and among what is recited to you are the two who commit it from among you," i.e., the immorality; the fa' entered the response because the sentence carries the sense of a condition.

Here al-ladhani refers to the male adulterer and the female adulteress by way of prevalence (taghlib). It was also said: the first verse concerns women specifically, both married and unmarried, and the second concerns men specifically, and the dual form is used to explain the two categories of men, those who are married and those who are not. So the punishment of women is confinement and the punishment of men is harm. Al-Nahhas chose this and narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Qurtubi narrated it from Mujahid and others and approved of it. Al-Suddi, Qatada and others said: the first verse concerns married women, and married men are included with them, and the second verse concerns the virgin man and woman. Al-Tabari preferred this, but al-Nahhas considered it weak and said: giving precedence to the feminine over the masculine is far-fetched.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: the meaning of this view is complete, but the wording of the verse conflicts with it. It was also said: confinement was for the adulterous woman only and not the man, so the woman was singled out for mention regarding confinement, then both were combined in harm. Qatada said: the woman would be confined and both would be harmed.

The exegetes differed in interpreting the harm (adha). It was said: rebuke and reproach. It was said: insult and harshness without reproach. It was said: verbal abuse and beating with sandals. Some people held that the harm is abrogated, like the confinement, and it was said: it is not abrogated, as already mentioned regarding confinement.

His words "But if they repent" (فإن تابا), i.e., from the immorality, and make amends in their conduct thereafter, "then leave them alone" (فأعرضوا عنهما), i.e., abandon them and refrain from harming them. This was before the revelation of the prescribed punishments, according to the disagreement already mentioned.

His words "Repentance is only upon God" (إنما التوبة على الله) are a resumption to explain that repentance is not accepted unconditionally, as His words "Ever Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful" (توابا رحيما) indicate, but is accepted from some and not others, as the Qur'anic composition here makes clear. So His words "repentance is only" (إنما التوبة) is the subject, whose predicate is His words "for those who do evil in ignorance" (للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة).

His words "upon God" (على الله) are connected to what the predicate carries of stability, or are connected to an omitted element that functions as a circumstantial clause according to those who permit placing a circumstantial adverbial phrase before its implicit governing element. It was also said the meaning is: repentance is by God's grace and mercy toward His servants. It was said: the meaning is that repentance is obligatory upon God, and this is according to the Mu'tazila, who make certain things obligatory upon God, among them accepting the repentance of penitents. It was also said: "upon" (على) here means "with" (عند), and it was said it means "from" (من). The community has agreed that repentance is an obligation upon believers, because of His words, "And turn to God in repentance, all of you, O believers." The majority held that it is valid from one sin without another, contrary to the Mu'tazila. It was also said that His words "upon God" are the predicate.

His words "for those who do evil" (للذين يعملون) are connected to what the predicate is connected to, or to an omitted element functioning as a circumstantial clause. Al-su' (السوء) here means the evil deed.

His words "in ignorance" (بجهالة) are connected to an omitted element functioning as a qualifier or circumstantial clause; i.e., they do it while characterized by ignorance, or as ignorant. Al-Qurtubi related from Qatada that he said: the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) agreed that every act of disobedience is in ignorance, whether deliberate or from unawareness.

It is reported from al-Dahhak and Mujahid that ignorance here means deliberateness. 'Ikrima said: all worldly affairs are ignorance, and from this is His words, "The life of this world is but play and amusement" (Muhammad: 36). Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is by the ignorance of their choosing fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure. It was also said: its meaning is that they do not know the reality of the punishment; this was mentioned by Ibn Furak and Ibn 'Atiyya considered it weak.

His words "then they repent soon" (ثم يتوبون من قريب) mean: before death approaches them, as His words indicate, "until, when death comes to one of them" (حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت). This was said by Abu Mijlaz, al-Dahhak, 'Ikrima and others. What is meant is before witnessing the angels and before the person is overcome by his soul. The "min" in His words "min qarib" is partitive; i.e., they repent during part of a short time, which is other than the moment of death's presence. It was also said: its meaning is before illness, but this is weak, indeed false, given what we have already mentioned, and given what Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it good), Ibn Majah, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman report from Ibn 'Umar from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle (yughargir)." It was also said: its meaning is that they repent while the sin is still recent, without persistence.

His words "those God will turn to in forgiveness" (فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم) are a promise from Him, the Exalted, that He will accept their repentance, after explaining that repentance is confined to them. His words "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds" (وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات) are an explicit statement of what was understood from restricting repentance, in what precedes, to those who did evil in ignorance and then repented soon. His words "until, when death comes to one of them" (حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت): "until" (حتى) is a particle of beginning, and the sentence mentioned after it is the endpoint of what precedes it. The presence of death means the presence of its signs, the patient reaching the state of the throes of death and becoming overcome in himself, preoccupied with his soul's departure from his body; this is the time of the death rattle mentioned in the previous hadith, which is when his soul reaches his throat, as al-Harawi said.

His words "He says: Indeed I have repented now" (قال إني تبت الآن), i.e., at the time of death's presence. His words "nor those who die while they are disbelievers" (ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار) are coordinated with the relative clause in His words "for those who do evil deeds," meaning: repentance is not for those, nor for those who die while disbelievers, though they have no repentance at all; they are mentioned as an intensification in explaining the non-acceptance of the repentance of one whom death has come upon, and that its existence is like its non-existence.

Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "And those of your women who commit immorality" (واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة), that he said: when a woman committed fornication she was confined in houses; if she died, she died, and if she lived, she lived, until the verse in Surat al-Nur was revealed: "The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each of them" (al-Nur: 2), and God made a way for them. So whoever did something was flogged and released. This has been related from him through several chains.

Abu Dawud in his Sunan and al-Bayhaqi reported from him regarding His words "And those of your women who commit immorality" up to "a way," then combining both together, "And the two of you who commit it among you, harm them both," then that was abrogated by the verse of flogging. Several of the Successors held the view of abrogation; Abu Dawud and al-Bayhaqi reported it from Mujahid, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu Dawud in his book on abrogation, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported it from Qatada, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported it from al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Hatim reported it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Jarir reported it from al-Suddi. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "And the two of you who commit it among you," that he said: when a man committed fornication he was harmed by reproach and beaten with sandals; then God revealed after this verse, "The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each one of them a hundred lashes" (al-Nur: 2), and if they were married they were stoned in the Sunna of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding "And the two of you who commit it among you": he said, the two men who do it. Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding it: meaning the two virgins.

Ibn Jarir reported from 'Ata' who said: the man and the woman. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Abu al-'Aliya regarding His words "Repentance is only upon God" up to the end of the verse: he said, this is for the believers; and regarding His words "Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds": he said, this is for the people of hypocrisy; "nor those who die while they are disbelievers": he said, this is for the people of polytheism.

Ibn Jarir reported similarly from al-Rabi'. 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatada who said: the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) agreed that everything disobeyed is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Abu al-'Aliya that the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) used to say: every sin a servant commits is ignorance. Ibn Jarir reported through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "Repentance is only upon God," up to the end of the verse, that he said: whoever does evil is ignorant, and from his ignorance is the doing of evil; "then they repent soon": he said, in life and health.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him that he said: "soon" is the period between the present and seeing the Angel of Death. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman reported from al-Dahhak who said: everything before death is soon for him; repentance is available between now and when he witnesses the Angel of Death, and if he repents when he sees the Angel of Death, that is not accepted for him.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Hasan who said: "soon" is what is before the death rattle. Many hadiths have been transmitted about the acceptance of a servant's repentance as long as he has not begun the death rattle; Ibn Kathir mentioned them in his tafsir, among them the hadith we mentioned earlier.

Some scholars held that the mentioned confinement and likewise the harm remain alongside the flogging, because there is no contradiction between them and combining them is possible.

Sibawayh said: the ya was dropped to distinguish declinable nouns from indeclinable demonstrative nouns. Abu 'Ali said: the ya was dropped for lightness.

The rest read al-ladhani with a single nun. It was also said: the first verse concerns women specifically, both married and unmarried, and the second concerns men specifically, and the dual form is used to explain the two categories of men, those who are married and those who are not. So the punishment of women is confinement and the punishment of men is harm. Al-Nahhas chose this and narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Qurtubi narrated it from Mujahid and others and approved of it. Al-Suddi, Qatada and others said: the first verse concerns married women, and married men are included with them, and the second verse concerns the virgin man and woman. Al-Tabari preferred this, but al-Nahhas considered it weak and said: giving precedence to the feminine over the masculine is far-fetched.

Some people held that the harm is abrogated, like the confinement, and it was said: it is not abrogated, as already mentioned regarding confinement.

This was before the revelation of the prescribed punishments, according to the disagreement already mentioned.

His words "Repentance is only upon God" (إنما التوبة على الله) are a resumption to explain that repentance is not accepted unconditionally, as His words "Ever Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful" (توابا رحيما) indicate, but is accepted from some and not others, as the Qur'anic composition here makes clear. It was also said the meaning is: repentance is by God's grace and mercy toward His servants. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "And the two of you who commit it among you," that he said: when a man committed fornication he was harmed by reproach and beaten with sandals; then God revealed after this verse, "The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each one of them a hundred lashes" (al-Nur: 2), and if they were married they were stoned in the Sunna of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding "And the two of you who commit it among you": he said, the two men who do it. Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding it: meaning the two virgins.

Ibn Jarir reported from 'Ata' who said: the man and the woman. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Abu al-'Aliya regarding His words "Repentance is only upon God" up to the end of the verse: he said, this is for the believers; and regarding His words "Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds": he said, this is for the people of hypocrisy; "nor those who die while they are disbelievers": he said, this is for the people of polytheism.

Ibn Jarir reported similarly from al-Rabi'. 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatada who said: the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) agreed that everything disobeyed is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Abu al-'Aliya that the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) used to say: every sin a servant commits is ignorance. Ibn Jarir reported through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "Repentance is only upon God," up to the end of the verse, that he said: whoever does evil is ignorant, and from his ignorance is the doing of evil; "then they repent soon": he said, in life and health.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him that he said: "soon" is the period between the present and seeing the Angel of Death. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman reported from al-Dahhak who said: everything before death is soon for him; repentance is available between now and when he witnesses the Angel of Death, and if he repents when he sees the Angel of Death, that is not accepted for him.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Hasan who said: "soon" is what is before the death rattle. Many hadiths have been transmitted about the acceptance of a servant's repentance as long as he has not begun the death rattle; Ibn Kathir mentioned them in his tafsir, among them the hadith we mentioned earlier.

This is connected to what preceded it concerning wives, and the purpose is to negate injustice against them. The address is to the guardians (awliyāʾ). The meaning of the verse becomes clear by knowing its occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), which al-Bukhārī and others narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾. He said: When a man died, his guardians had more right to his wife. If one of them wished, he would marry her; if they wished, they would marry her off; and if they wished, they would not marry her. So they had more right to her than her own family, and so it was revealed. In a wording of Abū Dāwūd from him regarding this verse: A man would inherit the wife of his relative and then withhold her (yaʿḍulu-hā) until she died or returned to him her dowry (ṣadāq). In a wording of Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim from him: If she was beautiful, he married her; and if she was ugly, he confined her until she died, so that he would inherit her. This occasion has been related in various wordings. The meaning of ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾ is: it is not lawful for you to take them by way of inheritance, claiming that you have more right to them than others, and keeping them for yourselves. And it is not lawful for you to withhold them (taʿḍulūhunna) from marrying others, in order to take their inheritance when they die, or so that they hand over their dowry to you when you permit them to marry.

Al-Zuhrī and Abū Mijlaz said: It was among their customs that when a man died leaving a wife, his son from another woman, or his closest agnate, would cast his garment over the woman, and he would become more entitled to her than she herself and than her guardians. If he wished, he would marry her without a dowry, except the dowry that the deceased had given her. If he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry, giving her nothing. And if he wished, he would withhold her so that she would ransom herself from him with what she had inherited from the deceased, or until she died and he inherited her. Then the verse was revealed. It was also said: The address is to the husbands of the women, when they confine them along with bad treatment, hoping to inherit them, or so that they will ransom themselves with part of their dowries. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah preferred this view, and said: The evidence for this is His words: ﴿except that they commit a clear immorality﴾. If a woman commits immorality, the guardian has no right to confine her until she departs with her wealth, by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the community; rather, that right belongs to the husband. Al-Ḥasan said: If a virgin commits fornication, she is to be flogged one hundred times and exiled, and she must return to her husband what she took from him.

Abū Qilābah said: If a man's wife commits adultery, there is no harm in his harming her and making things hard for her until she ransoms herself from him. Al-Suddī said: If they do that, then take their dowries.

Others said: The immorality (al-fāḥishah) is abusive speech with the tongue, and bad treatment is in word and deed. Mālik and a group of scholars said: The husband may take from a rebellious wife (nāshiz) all that she possesses.

All of this is based on the address in His words ﴿and do not withhold them﴾ being to the husbands. But you have understood from what we have mentioned about the occasion of revelation that the address in His words ﴿and do not withhold them﴾ is to those who were addressed by His words ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾. The meaning then is: it is not lawful for you to prevent them from marriage ﴿in order that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾, i.e., what those whom you inherit from had given them, ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, in which case it is permitted for you to keep them from husbands. And there is no concealing the strain (taʿassuf) in this, given that it is not permitted to confine a woman who has committed immorality from marrying and guarding her chastity from fornication. Just as making His words ﴿and do not withhold them﴾ an address to the guardians involves this strain, so making His words ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾ an address to the husbands involves a manifest strain, together with its contradiction of the occasion of revelation of the verse that we have mentioned. The better view is that the address in His words ﴿it is not lawful for you﴾ is to the Muslims. That is: it is not lawful for you, O community of Muslims, to inherit women against their will as the Jāhiliyyah did; and it is not lawful for you, O community of Muslims, to withhold your wives (taʿḍulū azwājakum), i.e., to keep them with you while you have no desire for them, but rather in order that you may take away part of the dowry you gave them, which they ransom themselves with to be released from confinement and from remaining under you. And despite your dislike of them, ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, it is permitted for you to separate from them (mukhāla‘ah) with part of what you have given them.

His words: مُبَيِّنَةٍ (mubayyinah, "clear"). Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with a kasrah under the yāʾ. The rest read it with a fatḥah. Ibn ʿAbbās read مُبِينَةٍ (mubīnah) with a kasrah under the bāʾ and a sukūn on the yāʾ, from abāna al-shayʾ, so it is mubīn.

His words: ﴿and live with them in kindness﴾: i.e., in what is known (maʿrūf) in this sharīʿah and among its people of good companionship. It is an address to the husbands or to what is more general than them, and it varies with differences among husbands in wealth, poverty, nobility and lowliness. ﴿But if you dislike them﴾ for some reason, other than committing immorality or rebelliousness, ﴿it may be that you dislike a thing while Allah places in it much good﴾: it may be that the matter will turn to what you love, namely the disappearance of dislike and its replacement with affection, and therefore there will be in that much good, more than continuing the companionship and having children. So the consequent here is omitted, indicated by its cause; that is: if you dislike them, then be patient, ﴿for it may be that you dislike a thing and Allah places in it much good.﴾

His words: ﴿and you have given one of them a great amount (qintār)﴾: its explanation has already been given in Āl ʿImrān, and what is meant here is abundant wealth, so do not take anything from it. It was said: this verse is muḥkam (not abrogated), and it was said: it is mansūkh (abrogated) by His words, may He be exalted, in Sūrat al-Baqarah: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229]. The better view is that all of it is muḥkam, and what is meant here is other than the one who seeks khulʿ; it is not lawful for her husband to take anything of what he gave her.

His words: ﴿Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ The interrogative is for denial and rebuke. The sentence confirms the first sentence, which contains the prohibition. His words: ﴿And how could you take it﴾ are a denial after a denial, containing the cause that requires prohibiting the taking: namely, al-ifḍāʾ (intimacy/going in together).

Al-Harawī said: It is when the two are under one blanket, whether he had intercourse or did not. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-ifḍāʾ is that a man and a woman are alone together, even if he has not had intercourse with her. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: al-ifḍāʾ in this verse is intercourse. The original meaning of al-ifḍāʾ in the language is mixing; it is said of a mixed thing that it is faḍāʾ, and it is said: the people are fawḍā and faḍāʾ, i.e., mixed together with no commander over them.

His words: ﴿and they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾ are coordinated with the sentence before it: i.e., the situation is that some of you have had intimacy with others, and they have taken from you a solemn covenant, which is the marriage contract. From it is His Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "You have taken them by the trust of Allah and have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah." It was also said: it is His words: ﴿either keep them in good fashion or release them with kindness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229]. And it was said: it is the children.

His words: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾: a prohibition against what the Jāhiliyyah used to do, marrying their fathers' wives after the fathers died. It begins an explanation of whom it is unlawful to marry among women and whom it is not unlawful.

Then He, glory be to Him, explained the reason for the prohibition, saying: ﴿Indeed, it was immorality and hatred and an evil way.﴾ These three attributes indicate that it is among the most grievous and most abominable of the prohibited things. The Jāhiliyyah used to call it nikāḥ al-maqt (the marriage of hatred). Thaʿlab said: I asked Ibn al-Aʿrābī about nikāḥ al-maqt, and he said: it is that a man marries his father's wife after he divorces her or she is widowed from him. This is also called al-ḍayzam. The root of al-maqt is hatred, from maqatahu, yamqutuhu, maqtan, so he is mamqūt and maqīt.

His words: ﴿except what has already passed﴾ is an exception that is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), i.e., but what has already passed, leave it and forsake it. It was said: illā here means baʿda, i.e., after what has passed. It was said: the meaning is "nor what has passed." It was said: it is a connected exception from His words ﴿what your fathers married﴾, conveying emphasis in prohibition by framing the speech as contingent on the impossible: that is, if it is possible for you to marry what has already passed, then marry, but nothing else is lawful for you. His words: ﴿and an evil way﴾: it functions like bi's (evil) in dispraise and in action, and the one being dispraised is omitted; that is, an evil way is the way of that marriage. It was said: it functions like the rest of the verbs, and in it is a pronoun referring back to what precedes it.

Al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who said: When Abū Qays ibn al-Aslat died, his son wanted to marry his wife, and this had been theirs in the Jāhiliyyah, so Allah revealed ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿIkrimah, who said: "This verse was revealed regarding Kubaysha bint Maʿmar ibn Maʿn ibn ʿĀṣim from the Aws. She was married to Abū Qays ibn al-Aslat. He died and left her, and his son became inclined toward her. So she came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'I did not inherit my husband, nor was I left to be married off.' So this verse was revealed."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Baylamānī regarding His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, and do not withhold them﴾, who said: These two verses were revealed, one of them concerning the affair of the Jāhiliyyah and the other concerning the affair of Islam. Ibn al-Mubārak said: ﴿to inherit women against their will﴾ is of the Jāhiliyyah, and ﴿do not withhold them﴾ is of Islam.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Abū Mālik regarding His words: ﴿and do not withhold them﴾, who said: Do not harm your wife so that she will ransom herself from you. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr narrated from Mujāhid, ﴿and do not withhold them﴾, meaning: that they marry their husbands, like al-ʿaḍl in Sūrat al-Baqarah. Ibn Jarīr narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said: ʿAḍl was among Quraysh in Makkah: a man would marry a noble woman, and perhaps she would not agree with him, so he would separate from her on condition that she not marry except with his permission. He would bring witnesses and have that written against her and have it witnessed. Then when a suitor proposed to her, if she gave him what he wanted and pleased him, he permitted her; otherwise he withheld her (ʿaḍalahā). We have already mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the explanation of the occasion what you have known.

Ibn Jarīr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿except that they commit a clear immorality﴾, who said: It is hatred and rebelliousness. If she does that, then it becomes lawful for him to take a ransom from her. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd narrated similarly from Qatādah. Ibn Jarīr also narrated similarly from al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Ibn Jarīr narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: Here, immorality is fornication. Ibn Jarīr narrated similarly from Abū Qilābah and Ibn Sīrīn.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from al-Suddī regarding His words: ﴿and live with them in kindness﴾, who said: Mix with them. Ibn Jarīr said: Some narrators distorted it; it is actually khāliqūhunna (be on good terms with them). Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿIkrimah, who said: Her right over you is good companionship, clothing, and reasonable provision. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Muqātil regarding ﴿and live with them in kindness﴾, meaning: their companionship in what is reasonable. ﴿But if you dislike them, it may be that you dislike a thing, and he divorces her, and she marries a man after him, and Allah places for him a child from her, and Allah places in her marriage much good.* Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The much good is that he shows compassion toward her, so she is provided for with her child, and Allah places in her child much good.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted something similar from al-Suddi. Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from al-Hasan something similar to what Muqatil said. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And if you desire to replace one spouse with another﴾ and the verse [continues], that he said: "If you dislike your wife and another woman pleases you, and you divorce this one and marry that one, then give this one her bridal gift (mahr), even if it is a qintar (a great treasure)."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu Ya'la transmitted that Umar forbade people to increase women's bridal gifts beyond four hundred dirhams. A woman of Quraysh confronted him and said: "Have you not heard what Allah revealed, saying: ﴿and you had given one of them a qintar﴾?" He said: "O Allah, forgive me! Everyone has more understanding than Umar." Then he mounted the pulpit and said: "O people, I had forbidden you to increase women's bridal gifts beyond four hundred dirhams. Whoever wishes to give from his wealth what he likes may do so." Abu Ya'la said: "I think he also said: 'Whoever is content in his soul, let him do so.'" Ibn Kathir said: "Its chain (isnad) is good and strong, and this story has been narrated with different wordings; this is one of them." (Al-Suyuti graded it as having a good chain.)

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he said: "al-ifda' (الإفْضاءُ) is intercourse (al-jima'), but Allah uses a euphemism (yakni)."

Abd ibn Humayd transmitted something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and they have taken from you a solemn covenant (mithaqan ghalizan)﴾, that he said: "al-ghalizh (الغَلِيظُ, the solemn) is either holding on with kindness (imsak bi-ma'ruf) or releasing with goodness (tasrih bi-ihsan)."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir transmitted from Qatadah something similar and said: "That used to be taken from the groom in the marriage contract: 'By Allah upon you, you will either keep her with kindness or release her with goodness.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Abi Mulaykah that Ibn Umar, whenever he married, would say: "I have married you according to what Allah has commanded: holding on with kindness or releasing with goodness."

Ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted from Anas ibn Malik something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted from Ibn Abbas something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted from Ikrimah and Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾, that they said: "You took them with the trust of Allah, and you made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he said: "It is the saying of the man: 'I have possessed (malaktu, مَلَكْتُ)'."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid that he said: "It is the word of marriage (kalimat al-nikah) by which their private parts are made lawful."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan transmitted regarding His words, exalted is He, ﴿And do not marry what your fathers married of women﴾ that it was revealed when Ibn Abi Qays ibn al-Aslat wished to marry his father's wife after his death.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿except what has already passed﴾: "except what was in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period)."

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan transmitted from al-Baraa, who said: "I met my maternal uncle, and he had the banner with him. I said: 'Where are you going?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a man who married his father's wife after him, and he commanded me to strike off his neck and take his wealth.'"
